question.problem: At a water bottle factory, every batch of $1\,000$ water bottles has $20$ water bottles (on average) on which the label is upside down. If an inspector comes to inspect the water bottles, what is the probability that they will find an upside down label before checking the $5$th bottle? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of bottles checked until a defect is found. On average, the chance of finding an upside down label on any water bottle is 

$$
p=\frac{20}{1\,000}=0.02.
$$

So, the number of bottles that the inspector checks before finding an upside down label can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success $p=0.02.$

So, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.02).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(1-0.02)^{x-1}(0.02) \\  & =(0.98)^{x-1}(0.02)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability of finding an upside down label before checking the $5$th bottle is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<5) & =P(X\in \{1,2,3,4\}) \\  & =f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+f(4) \\  & =(0.98)^{1-1}(0.02)+(0.98)^{2-1}(0.02)+(0.98)^{3-1}(0.02)+(0.98)^{4-1}(0.02) \\  & =(0.02)+(0.98)(0.02)+(0.98)^{2}(0.02)+(0.98)^{3}(0.02) \\  & =[1+0.98+(0.98)^{2}+(0.98)^{3}](0.02) \\  & ≈0.078\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
